proposal.summary: About 35% of /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}/complete requests return 500 on version 20260926-182749-105fb53. Every warn/error log line is the deliberate "injected drill fault" message. The release that added the fault-injection switch, and turned it on at 35% in compose.yaml, is the cause. The failure started right after that deploy. There is no sign of a database, network or resource fault.
proposal.root_cause_hypothesis: Commit 105fb53 adds complete_fault_rate() and a branch in task_complete() that raises RelayError("injected_fault", ..., 500) for a random fraction of requests. It also sets RELAY_FAULT_COMPLETE_5XX_RATE=0.35 in compose.yaml. The running release therefore fails about 35% of complete calls by design, which matches the observed 35.5%. The previous release, 829513a, has no such code path. The evidence does not show whether the fault was meant to run beyond the drill, but as deployed it makes the route unreliable for agents.

evidence_refs.finding: 105fb53 adds compose.yaml env RELAY_FAULT_COMPLETE_5XX_RATE: "0.35" (commented as an incident drill). It adds complete_fault_rate() and, in task_complete(), `if rate > 0 and random.random() < rate:` which logs a warning and raises RelayError("injected_fault", "Injected drill fault.", 500).

Roughly 170 WARN lines from 18:28:38Z to 18:30:36Z, all v=20260926-182749-105fb53 and all "injected drill fault: failing complete request (RELAY_FAULT_COMPLETE_5XX_RATE=0.35)". There are no database, connection or other application errors.

Version 20260926-182749-105fb53 (git_sha 105fb53) was released at 2026-09-26T18:28:19Z with previous_version 20260926-181002-829513a. The first injected-fault log line is at 18:28:38Z, about 20s after the deploy, and the alert has been active since 18:29:19Z.
The only version series with 5xx traffic is 20260926-182749-105fb53, at about 0.094 to 0.110 req/s. The errors are confined to the new release.
The alert (35.5% 5xx on the complete route, version 20260926-182749-105fb53) matches the configured injection rate of 0.35.

proposed_action.rationale: The failures come from code and config introduced by the running release (105fb53), not from infrastructure or a wedged process. The previous release, 829513a, does not contain the fault-injection path. Rolling back to it removes the fault and restores the complete route. A restart would not help, because RELAY_FAULT_COMPLETE_5XX_RATE=0.35 is set in compose.yaml. Escalation is not needed, because the cause is clear and the previous version is known from deploy history.

risks: Rolling back ends the HW4 incident drill early. The drill was intentional, so a human should confirm that is acceptable.

829513a also lacks the new test test_complete_fault_injection_switch. It is otherwise the immediately preceding release, so regression risk should be low, but it has not been checked against current traffic.
A rollback restarts the app container, which may briefly interrupt in-flight claim and complete requests.
Rolling back does not change the source tree or compose.yaml on main. A later redeploy from main would bring the fault back unless the env var is removed or set to 0.
proposal.verification_plan: After the rollback, check that GET /version reports 20260926-181002-829513a. Check that new "injected drill fault" WARN lines stop appearing in Loki. Check that the 5xx rate for /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}/complete falls to about 0 in Prometheus. Check that the tasks_terminal complete/error rate stops and the RelayClaimCompleteErrorRatioHigh alert resolves. Check that /health and /ready still return healthy and that queue depth and oldest-task age do not keep growing. Then remove RELAY_FAULT_COMPLETE_5XX_RATE from compose.yaml on main, or set it to 0, before the next release.
